query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A two‐stage thermomechanical treatment that refines the as-cast dual-phase lamellar colonies into a nanostructured dual heterogeneous microstructure will improve both the strength and room-temperature tensile ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloys with large lamellar colonies and numerous internal boundaries (as present in typical as-cast EHEAs).
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled two‐stage processing route (e.g., initial cryo‐rolling to store high strain energy followed by low-temperature warm‐rolling/annealing) to induce nanostructuring within the lamellar colonies.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature tensile deformation; processing must be optimized so the transformation does not lead to over-refinement or detrimental phase precipitation.
generation.structural_mediator: A dual heterogeneous microstructure consisting of retained lamellae interspersed with refined ultrafine/nanocrystalline domains that are coherent with the parent phases.
generation.mechanism: The refined regions act as crack arresters by blunting or deflecting microcrack propagation and provide a two-hierarchical constraint effect. This helps to both raise the yield strength (via grain refinement and possible solid solution strengthening) and improve ductility (through delayed microcrack coalescence and enhanced plasticity mechanisms) relative to the coarse, unmodified lamellar structure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the unmodified lamellar baseline, the processed alloy will exhibit an increase in yield strength and an appreciable improvement in tensile ductility at room temperature.
generation.baseline: Unmodified as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy lamellar colonies, which typically show high strength but limited ductility due to early microcrack initiation.
generation.boundary: The intervention is effective if the processing parameters (e.g., deformation amount in cryo-rolling and the temperature/duration of warm rolling or annealing) are precisely controlled to produce coherent nanostructured heterogeneities without introducing deleterious amorphization or coarse precipitates; the hypothesis may not hold if the alloy chemistry deviates significantly from that of the targeted eutectic HEAs.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative enhancements in strength and ductility and the exact nature of the nanostructured dual phases are subject to experimental verification. The optimal processing window and its sensitivity to composition require further study.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of EHEA samples from the same alloy composition. One set will receive the proposed two-stage treatment (cryo-rolling followed by controlled warm rolling/annealing) and the other will remain as-cast (baseline). Perform room-temperature tensile tests along with detailed microstructural characterization (grain size, phase distribution, and coherence of nanostructures).
measurements: Yield strength and work-of-strain (ductility) from tensile tests
Microstructural analysis via transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD)
Fractography to identify crack arresting or propagation mechanisms
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed samples do not show simultaneous improvement (i.e., a statistically significant increase) in both yield strength and room-temperature tensile ductility compared to the baseline, or if the microstructural analysis fails to reveal a well-defined coherent dual heterogeneous microstructure capable of impeding microcrack propagation, then the hypothesis is falsified.

Enhanced strength–ductility synergy in ultrafine-grained eutectic high-entropy alloys by inheriting microstructural lamellae

Abstract: Realizing improved strength–ductility synergy in eutectic alloys acting as in situ composite materials remains a challenge in conventional eutectic systems, which is why eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), a newly-emerging multi-principal-element eutectic category, may offer wider in situ composite possibilities. Here, we use an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA to engineer an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that deliberately inherits its composite lamellar nature by tailored thermo-mechanical processing to achieve property combinations which are not accessible to previously-reported reinforcement methodologies. The as-prepared samples exhibit hierarchically-structural heterogeneity due to phase decomposition, and the improved mechanical response during deformation is attributed to both a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism. Nanostructuring with Structural-Compositional Dual Heterogeneities Enhances Strength-Ductility Synergy in Eutectic High Entropy Alloy

Abstract: AbstractA lamellar (L12 + B2) AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA) was severely deformed by a novel hybrid-rolling process. During hybrid-rolling, the deformation was carried out in two stages, namely cryo-rolling followed by warm-rolling at 600 °C. The strain (ε) imparted in each of these steps was identical ~1.2, resulting in a total strain of ε~2.4 (corresponding to 90% reduction in thickness). The novel processing strategy resulted in an extremely heterogeneous microstructure consisting of retained lamellar and transformed nanocrystalline regions. Each of these regions consisted of different phases having different crystal structures and chemical compositions. The novel structure-composition dual heterogeneous microstructure originated from the stored energy of the cryo-rolling which accelerated transformations during subsequent low temperature warm-rolling.
